correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the published exact planar identity for the translative convex-hull ratio and independently derives the needed regular-polygon maximum. Central symmetrization preserves width and converts longest-chord length into twice the radial function. The central symmetral of a regular odd polygon is an explicitly scaled regular even polygon. In one edge-normal chamber the radial and perpendicular support functions are elementary cosines; the two even residue classes differ according to whether the perpendicular direction is a vertex or an edge normal. This proves the constant and monotone branches exactly, and division by the exact polygon area yields the stated three formulas.
risks: The numerical checker is not used as proof; all quantified steps are supplied analytically.

originality.rationale: The primary paper gives the general reduction, computes only the three-, four-, and five-gon extremal values, and explicitly asks whether regular polygons are extremizers for every number of sides. The new statement does not claim that open minimization theorem; it supplies the missing all-size closed evaluation of the regular benchmark and its directional phase. A later primary treatment of translative constant volume was inspected and does not state the formula. Known Radon-curve results account for the direction-independence in some residue classes but do not provide the complete numerical or 4k directional profile.

value.rationale: The regular-polygon value is the explicit target appearing in a published all-m extremal problem, so it is a motivated exact invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The result provides that target in closed form for every m, reveals a modulo-four phase in the directional geometry, recovers all published small cases, and gives the common asymptotic benchmark 1+4/pi. These exact values are directly useful for testing or proving the remaining extremal conjecture.
risks: The result evaluates the conjectured benchmark but does not settle the minimization problem for m>=6.
